The file uses standard AUR packaging practices throughout.

The PKGBUILD defines a standard AUR package for `omnidict-git`, an offline dictionary application. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` is appropriate here because the source is a VCS (git) checkout, and checksums are not applicable — this is a common and acceptable practice for git-based AUR packages.

The `pkgver()` function uses `git describe` to generate a version string from git tags, which is a standard method for versioning in git packages. The build process uses CMake to compile the application from the `app/` subdirectory, which aligns with typical Qt-based project builds. Dependencies and optional dependencies are reasonable for a Qt6 application with icon themes and Wayland support.

No suspicious network activity, obfuscated code, or unauthorized system modifications are present. The package installs only into `$pkgdir`, and post-install hooks are absent, indicating no system-wide changes. All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices.
</details>
